<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

On ROCm, the existing `residual_gate_add` Triton kernels embed NVIDIA PTX (`cvt.rn.bf16.f32` / `cvt.rn.f16.f32`, constraint `"=h"`). AMDGPU does not support the `h` register class, so LLVM aborts during compilation instead of raising a Python exception. The diffusion worker can therefore terminate during denoising before the eager fallback is reached.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

This PR adds a dedicated ROCm Triton fast path while preserving the existing CUDA implementation.

- CUDA keeps the existing JIT/custom-op path and NVIDIA PTX rounding helper, now named `_cuda_round16_f32`.
- ROCm uses a separate custom op and Triton kernels for flat and transposed layouts.
- The ROCm flat kernel also handles batched `[B, 1, D]` gates, including LTX-2's strided AdaLN views.
- ROCm BF16 rounding uses `round_bf16_to_fp32`.
- ROCm FP16 rounding uses opaque `v_cvt_f16_f32` inline assembly because a normal FP32 → FP16 → FP32 cast can be folded away by Triton.
- CUDA and ROCm use separate predicates and rounding helpers. Unsupported inputs continue to use the eager fallback.
- Existing residual-gate tests now dispatch to the appropriate backend, with a regression test ensuring HIP never enters the CUDA/PTX path.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

On gfx1151, the ROCm path was compared against the eager reference with exact comparison for FP16 and BF16.

Coverage includes FP16/BF16/FP32, full/row-broadcast/per-token/batched gates, transposed layouts, storage offsets, graph/compile paths, and unsupported-input fallback.



## Speed Tests

gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), ROCm 7.2.4, PyTorch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0.
Row-broadcast gate, wall-clock time per call:

| dtype | shape | eager | ROCm path | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | `[1, 4096, 3072]` | 560.6 µs | 333.6 µs | 1.68x |
| bf16 | `[1, 4202, 3072]` | 568.8 µs | 341.6 µs | 1.67x |
| fp16 | `[1, 4096, 3072]` | 563.5 µs | 330.5 µs | 1.71x |
| fp16 | `[1, 4202, 3072]` | 572.3 µs | 339.4 µs | 1.69x |

These measurements cover the row-broadcast path only; the transposed ROCm path has not been independently profiled on AMD, so no speedup is claimed for that layout.

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Test Results

| Validation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `residual_gate_add` standalone | ROCm process aborts while compiling NVIDIA PTX | ROCm Triton path matches eager |
| Residual-gate test cases | Process terminated at the first case | All 55 ROCm residual-gate cases pass |
| Unsupported ROCm inputs | Eager fallback only | Unsupported inputs still use the eager fallback |

Only gfx1151 was validated locally. gfx942 and gfx950 remain for AMD CI.
CUDA was not run locally; its implementation was preserved unchanged.

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

nodes.body:
Thanks for working on this. From the ROCm side, I think the optimization demonstrated here is still valuable even after #42391.

The current results show that the residual_gate_add operation does not fundamentally need to fall back to eager mode on HIP — the PTX-specific rounding can be replaced with a ROCm-compatible implementation while preserving bit-exact results, with a meaningful performance benefit (~1.7x at the kernel level and ~4% in Qwen-Image denoising on gfx1151).

That said, I think we should align with the dispatch structure introduced by #42391 rather than mixing CUDA/PTX and ROCm-specific logic into the same path.

My preference would be:

* Keep the existing CUDA/JIT CUDA path unchanged.
* Keep the current fallback as the safe default for unsupported backends/configurations.
* Add a dedicated ROCm Triton fast path for the supported HIP cases, with correctness tests against the eager implementation.
* Avoid making the CUDA implementation more complex solely to accommodate HIP.

This gives us a clean backend separation while still allowing ROCm to benefit from the optimization demonstrated in this PR.

 from sglang.srt.utils.custom_op import register_custom_op

@@ -76,7 +77,7 @@ def _residual_gate_add_cuda_impl(
 
 
 @triton.jit
-def _round16_f32(x, IS_BF16: tl.constexpr):
+def _cuda_round16_f32(x, IS_BF16: tl.constexpr):
     if IS_BF16:
         bits = tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
             "cvt.rn.bf16.f32 $0, $1;", "=h,r", [x], dtype=tl.int16, is_pure=True, pack=1

@@ -174,6 +175,161 @@ def _residual_gate_add_transposed(residual, update, gate):
     return out
 
 
+@triton.jit
+def _rocm_round16_f32(x, IS_BF16: tl.constexpr):
+    """Round to 16-bit precision on AMD without NVIDIA PTX."""
+    if IS_BF16:
+        return round_bf16_to_fp32(x)
+    bits = tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        "v_cvt_f16_f32 $0, $1",
+        "=v,v",
+        [x],
+        dtype=tl.int16,
+        is_pure=True,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+    return bits.to(tl.float16, bitcast=True).to(tl.float32)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _rocm_store16(out_ptr, offs, value_f32, mask, IS_BF16: tl.constexpr):
+    if IS_BF16:
+        value = value_f32.to(tl.bfloat16)
+    else:
+        value = value_f32.to(tl.float16)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + offs, value, mask=mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _rga_rocm_flat(
+    out,
+    res,
+    upd,
+    gate,
+    numel,
+    hid,
+    batch_numel,
+    MODE: tl.constexpr,
+    IS_BF16: tl.constexpr,
+    IS_16: tl.constexpr,
+    BLK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    offs = pid * BLK + tl.arange(0, BLK).to(tl.int64)
+    mask = offs < numel
+    rv = tl.load(res + offs, mask=mask)
+    uv = tl.load(upd + offs, mask=mask)
+    if MODE == 1:
+        gv = tl.load(gate + (offs % hid), mask=mask)
+    elif MODE == 2:
+        gv = tl.load(gate + (offs // hid), mask=mask)
+    elif MODE == 3:
+        # One [D] gate row per batch: index by batch, then hidden position.
+        gv = tl.load(gate + (offs // batch_numel) * hid + (offs % hid), mask=mask)
+    else:
+        gv = tl.load(gate + offs, mask=mask)
+    if IS_16:
+        value = rv.to(tl.float32) + _rocm_round16_f32(
+            uv.to(tl.float32) * gv.to(tl.float32), IS_BF16
+        )
+        _rocm_store16(out, offs, value, mask, IS_BF16)
+    else:
+        tl.store(out + offs, rv + uv * gv, mask=mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _rga_rocm_transposed(
+    out,
+    res,
+    upd,
+    gate,
+    tokens,
+    hid: tl.constexpr,
+    IS_BF16: tl.constexpr,
+    IS_16: tl.constexpr,
+    TILE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid_t = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    pid_h = tl.program_id(1).to(tl.int64)
+    pid_b = tl.program_id(2).to(tl.int64)
+    t = pid_t * TILE + tl.arange(0, TILE).to(tl.int64)
+    h = pid_h * TILE + tl.arange(0, TILE).to(tl.int64)
+    mt = t < tokens
+    mh = h < hid
+    gv = tl.load(gate + h, mask=mh, other=0.0)
+    base = pid_b * tokens * hid
+    mask = mh[:, None] & mt[None, :]
+    roffs = h[:, None] * tokens + t[None, :]
+    rv = tl.load(res + base + roffs, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    uv = tl.load(upd + base + t[None, :] * hid + h[:, None], mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    if IS_16:
+        value = rv.to(tl.float32) + _rocm_round16_f32(
+            uv.to(tl.float32) * gv[:, None].to(tl.float32), IS_BF16
+        )
+        _rocm_store16(out, base + roffs, value, mask, IS_BF16)
+    else:
+        tl.store(out + base + roffs, rv + uv * gv[:, None], mask=mask)
+
+
+def _residual_gate_add_rocm_triton(residual, update, gate):
+    out = torch.empty_strided(
+        residual.shape, residual.stride(), dtype=residual.dtype, device=residual.device
+    )
+    is_bf16 = residual.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    is_16 = residual.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
+    if _is_transposed_dense_residual(residual, update, gate):
+        _, tokens, hidden = residual.shape
+        # Tile/warp sizes reused from the CUDA transposed kernel; not
+        # independently tuned or profiled on AMD GPUs.
+        tile = (
+            16
+            if residual.numel() <= 65536
+            else 64
+            if residual.numel() >= 1 << 20
+            else 32
+        )
+        warps = 4 if tile == 16 else 8
+        _rga_rocm_transposed[
+            (triton.cdiv(tokens, tile), triton.cdiv(hidden, tile), residual.shape[0])
+        ](
+            out,
+            residual,
+            update,
+            gate,
+            tokens,
+            hidden,
+            is_bf16,
+            is_16,
+            TILE=tile,
+            num_warps=warps,
+        )
+        return out
+
+    numel = residual.numel()
+    hidden = residual.shape[-1]
+    mode = _gate_mode(residual, gate)
+    if mode == 3:
+        # AdaLN unbind views have gaps between batch rows. Only copy the small
+        # [B, 1, D] gate, never expand it across the token dimension.
+        gate = gate.contiguous()
+    block = 256 if numel <= 8192 else 1024
+    _rga_rocm_flat[(triton.cdiv(numel, block),)](
+        out,
+        residual,
+        update,
+        gate,
+        numel,
+        hidden,
+        numel // residual.shape[0],
+        mode,
+        is_bf16,
+        is_16,
+        BLK=block,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    return out
+
+
 @register_custom_op(
     op_name="diffusion_residual_gate_add",
     mutates_args=[],
@@ -191,6 +347,18 @@ def _residual_gate_add_custom_op(
         return _residual_gate_add_cuda_impl(residual, update, gate)
 
 
+@register_custom_op(
+    op_name="diffusion_residual_gate_add_rocm",
+    mutates_args=[],
+    fake_impl=_fake_impl,
+)
+def _residual_gate_add_rocm_custom_op(
+    residual: torch.Tensor, update: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    with torch.cuda.device(residual.device):
+        return _residual_gate_add_rocm_triton(residual, update, gate)
+
+
 def _gate_mode(residual: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor) -> int:
     """0 = full, 1 = shared row, 2 = per-token, 3 = one row per batch."""
     if gate.shape == residual.shape:
@@ -241,12 +409,11 @@ def _is_transposed_dense_residual(
     )
 
 
-def can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda(
+def _can_use_residual_gate_add_common(
     residual: torch.Tensor, update: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor
 ) -> bool:
     return (
-        torch.version.hip is None
-        and residual.dtype in _SUPPORTED_DTYPES
+        residual.dtype in _SUPPORTED_DTYPES
         and residual.dtype == update.dtype
         and residual.dtype == gate.dtype
         and residual.is_cuda
@@ -270,6 +437,24 @@ def can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda(
     )
 
 
+def can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda(
+    residual: torch.Tensor, update: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor
+) -> bool:
+    """Return whether the NVIDIA-only JIT/Triton dispatch can handle the input."""
+    return torch.version.hip is None and _can_use_residual_gate_add_common(
+        residual, update, gate
+    )
+
+
+def can_use_residual_gate_add_rocm(
+    residual: torch.Tensor, update: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor
+) -> bool:
+    """Return whether the dedicated ROCm Triton path can handle the input."""
+    return torch.version.hip is not None and _can_use_residual_gate_add_common(
+        residual, update, gate
+    )
+
+
 def residual_gate_add_cuda(
     residual: torch.Tensor, update: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor
 ) -> torch.Tensor:
@@ -278,19 +463,30 @@ def residual_gate_add_cuda(
     return _residual_gate_add_custom_op(residual, update, gate)
 
 
+def residual_gate_add_rocm(
+    residual: torch.Tensor, update: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if not can_use_residual_gate_add_rocm(residual, update, gate):
+        raise RuntimeError("unsupported input for residual_gate_add ROCm")
+    return _residual_gate_add_rocm_custom_op(residual, update, gate)
+
+
 def residual_gate_add(
     residual: torch.Tensor, update: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor
 ) -> torch.Tensor:
-    """Use the bit-exact fast path for supported layouts, otherwise eager."""
-    if residual.dtype in _BIT_EXACT_DTYPES and can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda(
-        residual, update, gate
-    ):
-        return _residual_gate_add_custom_op(residual, update, gate)
+    """Use the backend's bit-exact fast path for supported layouts, otherwise eager."""
+    if residual.dtype in _BIT_EXACT_DTYPES:
+        if can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda(residual, update, gate):
+            return _residual_gate_add_custom_op(residual, update, gate)
+        if can_use_residual_gate_add_rocm(residual, update, gate):
+            return _residual_gate_add_rocm_custom_op(residual, update, gate)
     return residual + update * gate
 
 
 __all__ = [
     "can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda",
+    "can_use_residual_gate_add_rocm",
     "residual_gate_add",
     "residual_gate_add_cuda",

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for working on this. From the ROCm side, I think the optimization demonstrated here is still valuable even after #42391.

The current results show that the residual_gate_add operation does not fundamentally need to fall back to eager mode on HIP — the PTX-specific rounding can be replaced with a ROCm-compatible implementation while preserving bit-exact results, with a meaningful performance benefit (~1.7x at the kernel level and ~4% in Qwen-Image denoising on gfx1151).

That said, I think we should align with the dispatch structure introduced by #42391 rather than mixing CUDA/PTX and ROCm-specific logic into the same path.

My preference would be:

* Keep the existing CUDA/JIT CUDA path unchanged.
* Keep the current fallback as the safe default for unsupported backends/configurations.
* Add a dedicated ROCm Triton fast path for the supported HIP cases, with correctness tests against the eager implementation.
* Avoid making the CUDA implementation more complex solely to accommodate HIP.

This gives us a clean backend separation while still allowing ROCm to benefit from the optimization demonstrated in this PR.
